['[CHECKS AND MAINTENANCE]
Daily maintenance and periodic maintenance/inspection ensure reliable robot performance for extended periods of time. 
(1) Daily maintenance 
- Before operating the system each day, clean each part of the system and check the system parts for any damage or cracks. Also, check the following: 
(a) Before operation 
- Check the cable connected to the teach pendant for excessive twisting. Check the controller and peripheral devices for abnormalities. 
(b) After operation 
- At the end of operation, return the robot to the specified position, and then turn off the controller. Clean each part, and check for any damage or cracks. If the ventilation port of the controller is dusty, clean it. 
(2) Check after one month 
- Check that the fan is rotating normally. If the fan has dirt and dust built up, clean the fan according to step 
(3) described below for inspection to be performed every 6 months. 
(3) Periodic inspection performed every six months 
- Remove any dirt and dust from the inside of the cabinet. Wipe off dirt and dust from the fan. 
(4) Battery daily check 
- Replace the battery on the front panel of the main board every 4 years. Please refer to the Section 7.11. 
(5) Maintenance tools 
The following maintenance tools are recommended: 
(a) Measuring instruments 
AC/DC voltmeter (A digital voltmeter is sometimes required.) 
- Oscilloscope with a frequency range of 5 MHz or higher, two channels 
(b) Tools 
- Cross-head screwdrivers: Large, medium, and small 
- Straight-head screwdrivers: Large, medium, and small 
- Nut driver set (Metric) 
- Pliers

And the specific descriptions of CE and NRTL controller have notifications in this manual.

Before you enter the robot working area, be sure to turn off the power to the controller or press the EMERGENCY STOP button on the operator's panel or teach pendant. 
Otherwise, you could injure personnel or damage equipment.", '[SAFETY OF THE MAINTENANCE ENGINEER]
(4) When entering the area enclosed by the safety fence, the worker must check the whole robot system in order to make sure no dangerous situations exist. In case the worker needs to enter the safety area whilst a dangerous situation exists, extreme care must be taken, and whole robot system status must be carefully monitored. 
(5) Before the maintenance of the pneumatic system is started, the supply pressure should be shut off and the pressure in the piping should be reduced to zero. 
(6) Before the start of maintenance work, check that the robot and its peripheral equipment are all in the normal operating condition. 
(7) Do not operate the robot in the automatic operation while anybody is in the robot operating space. 
(8) When you maintain the robot alongside a wall or instrument, or when multiple users are working nearby, make certain that their escape path is not obstructed. 
(9) When a tool is mounted on the robot, or when any movable device other than the robot is installed, such as belt conveyor, pay careful attention to its motion. 
(10) If necessary, have a user who is familiar with the robot system stand beside the operator panel and observe the work being performed. If any danger arises, the user should be ready to press the EMERGENCY STOP button at any time. 
(11) When replacing a part, please contact your local FANUC representative. If a wrong procedure is followed, an accident may occur, causing damage to the robot and injury to the user. 
(12) When replacing or reinstalling components, take care to prevent foreign material from entering the system. 
(13) When handling each unit or printed circuit board in the controller during inspection, turn off the circuit breaker to protect against electric shock. 
- If there are two cabinets, turn off the both circuit breaker. 
(14) A part should be replaced with a part recommended by FANUC. If other parts are used, malfunction or damage would occur. Especially, a fuse that is not recommended by FANUC should not be used. Such a fuse may cause a fire. 
(15) When restarting the robot system after completing maintenance work, make sure in advance that there is no person in the operating space and that the robot and the peripheral equipment are not abnormal. 
(16) When a motor or brake is removed, the robot arm should be supported with a crane or other equipment beforehand so that the arm would not fall during the removal. 
(17) Whenever grease is spilled on the floor, it should be removed as quickly as possible to prevent dangerous falls. 
(18) The following parts are heated. If a maintenance user needs to touch such a part in the heated state, the user should wear heat-resistant gloves or use other protective tools. 
- Servo motor 
- Inside the controller 
- Reducer 
- Gearbox 
- Wrist unit 
(19) Maintenance should be done under suitable light. Care must be taken that the light would not cause any danger. 
(20) When a motor, reducer, or other heavy load is handled, a crane or other equipment should be used to protect maintenance workers from excessive load. Otherwise, the maintenance workers would be severely injured.']

question: What is the recommended type of cable to improve resistance to electrical noise in a FA environment according to the Fanuc R-30iB controller manual?
answer:
Fonte documentale: connections.pdf (Pagina: 190), (200)

Secondo il manuale di controllo del FA-R30iB, per migliorare la resistenza alle interferenze elettromagnetiche è raccomandato utilizzare un cavo con le seguenti caratteristiche:

- Struttura: Gruppo schermato (shield), disponibile una fila di drenaggio.
- Conduttore: Filo AWG26 annealed copper twist, sheath spessa 0.8 mm e diametro esterno di 6.7 mm ± 0.3 mm.
- Classi antincendio: Conformità UL1581 VW-1
- Resistenza all'olio: Conformità agli standard interni Fanuc equivalenti alle coperte elettriche resistenti all'olio.
- Flessibilità: Può resistere fino a 1,000,000 volte di flessione con un raggio di curvatura di 50 mm (test di flessione U-shaped).

Si dovrebbe utilizzare il connettore TM21CP-88P (numero di modello: 03), prodotto dalla HIROSE ELECTRIC CO., LTD. per questo tipo di cavo. Inoltre, è consigliato tagliare una parte della guaina del cavo per esporre lo schermo e fissarlo all'anodo terra utilizzando un fermaglio a cavo per migliorare la protezione contro le interferenze elettromagnetiche.

question: What are the conditions that must be met for the type of Ethernet cable used in the R-30iB system?
answer:
1. Supports both 100BASE-TX and 1000BASE-T interfaces, as specified on page 195 of connections.pdf.
2. Includes an auto-negotiation function for automatic configuration of the connection parameters.
3. Capable of store-and-forward switching to ensure reliable data transmission.
4. Provides flow control to manage data transfer and prevent buffer overflow.
5. Should be used in a dust-proof cabinet to protect against environmental factors like dust or oil mist, as mentioned on page 195 of connections.pdf.

question: What is the difference between the 'WARNING' and 'CAUTION' symbols according to the Fanuc R-30iB controller manual?
answer:
1. **Formato**: "WARNING" è tipicamente utilizzato per segnalare situazioni che possono causare danni immediati o gravi conseguenze, mentre "CAUTION" indica avvertenze meno severe ma comunque importanti da prendere in considerazione.
2. **Severità**: Il livello di rischio è maggiore per i messaggi con il simbolo "WARNING", suggerendo che devono essere prese immediatamente misure, mentre "CAUTION" può indicare una minore preoccupazione ma comunque richiede attenzione.
3. **Contenuto**: I messaggi associati al "WARNING" spesso discutono di condizioni o azioni che possono portare a danni fisici, guasti significativi dell'attrezzatura o perdite gravi, mentre i messaggi con il simbolo "CAUTION" potrebbero riguardare problemi operativi meno critici o precauzioni per mantenere l'integrità dell'attrezzatura.

3. Check the wires connecting between the teach pendant and the emergency stop board (CRS36) for continuity. If an open wire is found, replace the entire harness. (Fonte: troubleshooting_alarms.pdf, Pagina: 21)
4. Perform a complete controller back-up to save all your programs and settings before proceeding with further actions. (Fonte: troubleshooting_alarms.pdf, Pagina: 37)
5. Replace the emergency stop board. (Fonte: troubleshooting_alarms.pdf, Pagina: 21, combinato con SRVO-213)
6. If SRVO-007 is also issued together with SRVO-213, consider that a fuse may have blown and follow the same actions as for SRVO-213. (Fonte: troubleshooting_alarms.pdf, Pagina: 27)

question: What are the steps to follow if the alarm SRVO-050 Collision Detect occurs and an overload on the robot is suspected?
answer:
1. Check whether the robot has collided or if there is a factor that increased the mechanical load on the corresponding axis.
2. Verify that the load settings are valid.
3. Inspect to ensure that the brake of the corresponding axis is released. If not, release it by checking for clack sounds or vibrations from the brake mechanism.
4. If the brake remains engaged and no disconnection issue in connectors CNJ1A-CNJ6 is found:
    a. Check the continuity of both the robot connection cable and the internal power/brake cable for any faults.
    b. Replace either the 6-Axis servo amplifier or the corresponding servo motor if there are issues with these components.
5. If the load weight exceeds the rated range:
    a. Reduce it to within the specified limits, as high torque requirements can cause motors to fail in following commands and trigger alarms.
6. Confirm that the voltage input to the controller is within the rated voltage and there are no phase losses. For CRR38A or CRR38B connectors:
    a. Ensure the line voltage does not exceed 210 VAC; if it's higher, check the mainline voltage as well since this can affect torque output and potentially cause alarms due to low motor performance.
7. If issues persist after these checks, consider replacing the servo amplifier or corresponding servo motor according to steps (6) and (7).
